questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Love for italian culture, cuisine and the location itself.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Rather difficult at first, but thankfully I got good guidance from the Erasmus coordinators. Also, I had several friends also on exchange, which made it easier for all of us as we could share tips and tricks for getting into the rhythm of studying in Milan.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Erasmus coordinator Massimo Costa was helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Recieved housing through the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nice, cheap and easy. Note however that there are somewhat strict rules. For example I was not allowed to keep my race bike in the room, which was a major letdown. Also no late-night visits.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was easy and online, but it lacked confirmation. I had no clue if I had been accepted to my chosen course until halfway through the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Fellow students in class (local students) were helpful. The application process was also rather intuitive

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont worry about not receiving confirmation right away. It will work out in the end as registrations seem to be pretty flexible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels varied but in general were lower than my sending institution

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was different. Small-scale, in class presentations and discussions as well as mandatory attendance for some courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Digital Society
Comparative Political Systems
European Monetary and Economic Law
Multi-level Legal System

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Digital society was a good course. As was multi-level legal system, though it was difficult for me as I have no background in law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A winter jacket in December. It gets cold in Milan.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food more expensive than expected and also more expensive relative to other parts of Italy. Housing was, in my case, cheap, as I got a room through the university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To my knowledge not many.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not attend

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on day trips to the surrounding cities. Como is nice for hiking and swimming. Genova has amazing food. Bologna is worth a visit. Take the train, use the Trenitalia app.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There were many Exchange students and in general it was an international environment. The local students were very friendly, helpful and talkative. No problem adjusting whatsoever.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to approach the Italians, they are very friendly and welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The administrative processes. As I've mentioned, the lack of confirmation when signing up for classes and the somewhat lackluster introduction to the whereabouts of the campus and the online platforms needed for the classes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food. The coffee. The people, both Italian and international. Also, the drinking culture is very moderated (compared to Denmark) which made for many fun (and more controlled) nights out.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't expect everything to go as planned
2. Go for small trips in the weekend 
3. Talk to the professors, they are helpful and take an interest in you if you reach out

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The language course provided by the host institution is very time consuming and (in my opinion) not worth the time, especially as it is online and takes place in the evening.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Overcoming the difficulties of new academic causes (in my case in a new field; law) and having success at the exams. Also, meeting new people and making friends from across Europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be uncomfortable not knowing how exactly things are going to work out. A lot is challenging in the beginning, both socially and academically.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
